svg.title: UHF RFID band map — Africa has no single band
svg.desc: A frequency map of the UHF RFID bands across Africa. Most of the continent mirrors the European Union 865-868 MHz band under the ETSI EN 302 208 framework — Egypt, Kenya and Morocco all sit there — while South Africa uses 915.4-919 MHz under ICASA at up to 4 W EIRP, roughly 50 MHz higher and inside the upper part of the United States 902-928 MHz FCC band. The two African allocations are about 50 MHz apart, so there is no single African band and passive inlays must be tuned for the destination country. HF and NFC cards at 13.56 MHz are global and unaffected.
svg.text: GET THE BAND RIGHT — AFRICA HAS NO SINGLE BAND
The UHF allocation depends on the country — EU 865-868 stock reads short on a South African portal
REFERENCE BANDS
EU 865-868 MHz
ETSI EN 302 208
US 902-928 MHz · FCC Part 15
AFRICAN ALLOCATIONS — SAME CONTINENT, DIFFERENT BAND
~50 MHz apart — same continent, different band
◀ EU lower band
US upper band ▶
Egypt · Kenya · Morocco — and most of the continent
865-868 MHz (EN 302 208 basis; Egypt & Morocco 2 W e.r.p.)
South Africa
915.4-919 MHz · ICASA · up to 4 W EIRP
There is no “African band” — the UHF allocation depends on the destination country
Most of North, East and West Africa mirrors the EU 865-868 MHz band; South Africa sits ~50 MHz higher at 915.4-919 MHz.
An inlay tuned for Cairo or Nairobi reads short on a Johannesburg portal — and the reverse is just as true.
Name the destination country on the RFQ and inlays are tuned to match. HF / NFC cards at 13.56 MHz are global.
Sources: GS1 RAIN UHF allocations; ICASA (South Africa); NTRA (Egypt); Communications Authority (Kenya). Confirm your destination band before ordering.
Bands are per-country and can change — a serious supplier confirms the destination allocation before quoting, never guesses.
